findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify HOW the credential is stored on the transport for the PAT-repr test — e.g., 'use `build_client_from_settings` + monkeypatch (mirroring the existing TLS tests) so the PAT flows through settings into the real transport, then assert `repr(transport)` does not include the PAT value; or document that the transport constructor must be extended to accept and store a `_pat` field' — the current plan leaves this mechanism unspecified, which will produce either a vacuous test or an unintended API change.
evidence: Plan AC 1: 'the PAT-repr test constructs a transport that ACTUALLY carries a credential'
transport.py:217-232: `JiraDataCenterTransport.__init__` signature is `(self, *, client, project, resolved_statuses=None)` — no PAT field
The existing TLS tests use `_built_client_kwargs(monkeypatch, ...)` which drives `build_client_from_settings` and captures kwargs — the PAT is on the settings/client, NOT on the transport object
Mutation check requires a `__repr__` that can leak 'the credential' — but there is no credential attribute on the transport to leak
findings.finding: Item 1's fix mechanism is unspecified at the critical point: `JiraDataCenterTransport.__init__` accepts only `client`, `project`, and `resolved_statuses` — there is no PAT parameter. The plan says 'constructs a transport that ACTUALLY carries a credential' but does not say HOW the credential gets onto the transport object. An implementer has at least three options (add a `_pat` field to the constructor, use `build_client_from_settings` + monkeypatch as the existing TLS tests do, or inject a client object whose repr would expose the PAT), and they have meaningfully different blast radii and semantics. The mutation check ('adding a `__repr__` that leaks it') presupposes a stored credential field on the transport, which does not currently exist. Without specifying whether to (a) extend the transport constructor to hold the PAT, (b) use `build_client_from_settings` + monkeypatch to build a real transport and assert the PAT passed via settings doesn't appear in `repr`, or (c) inject a credential-bearing fake client, the test will either be vacuous (option c tests only the client's repr, not the transport's) or require an unintended production change (option a changes the DC transport API).
findings.location: Acceptance criteria — item 1 / test_jira_dc_transport_heldout.py:106-111
scenarios: Implementer adds `_pat=None` to the constructor as a convenience: this changes the production API surface unnecessarily and may conflict with other tests that construct `JiraDataCenterTransport` without a PAT.

Implementer injects a fake client that stores the PAT and checks `repr(t)` doesn't include it: the transport's `repr` is `<...JiraDataCenterTransport object at 0x...>` by default regardless — the test passes vacuously (same defect as before) if no custom `__repr__` is added to the transport.

Implementer uses `build_client_from_settings` + monkeypatch (the pattern already used by TLS tests in the same file): this would test the `repr` of a transport whose inner `_client` carries the PAT — a reasonable approach, but the credential is on `self._client`, so the test is really checking that `repr` doesn't recurse into the client's attributes.
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror the existing `_built_client_kwargs` pattern: monkeypatch `_jira_client_class` to capture the constructed client, then call `build_client_from_settings(settings_with_pat)`, construct `JiraDataCenterTransport(client=captured_client, project='DC')`, and assert `'pat-xyz' not in repr(transport)`. This requires adding a `__repr__` to `JiraDataCenterTransport` (which is the point — the mutation check adds one that leaks it). Clarify in the AC that the `__repr__` addition is to the production class, not a test helper.
